5. **Start four workspaces** from the new `origin/main`:

   - `rog-env-design` (`docs/env-prefix-design`)

   - `rog-utilities` (`feat/rules-utilities`, plan first)

   - I rebuild `main` and verify after each merge.
   - My helper files move to `/tmp/opencode/rog/`.

# Isolated environment for the hk reproduction. Source it: `. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh`
# Everything hk, mise, git and pklr write by default lands under $R, except mise's install store, which is shared
# on purpose (hk 2.8.0 / 2.11.0, node, bun binaries are read from it; `mise install hk@2.11.0` added to it).

# Helpers for the hk reproduction. Source after env.sh.
SRC=[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-loading   # read only: objects of origin/main are fetched from it
MODULES=$SRC/node_modules                # symlinked into the scratch checkouts (read only)

# setup <run dir> <hk version>: bare origin, main clone pinned to that hk, hooks installed, two linked worktrees
setup() {
  local D=$1 V=$2
  rm -rf "$D"; mkdir -p "$D"
  git init -q --bare "$D/origin.git"
  git -C "$D/origin.git" fetch -q "$SRC" refs/remotes/origin/main:refs/heads/main
  git -C "$D/origin.git" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
  git clone -q "$D/origin.git" "$D/main"
  # node_modules is a symlink, which the `node_modules/` pattern in .gitignore does not match
  echo node_modules >> "$D/main/.git/info/exclude"
  ln -s "$MODULES" "$D/main/node_modules"
  if [ "$V" != 2.8.0 ]; then
    sed -i "s/^hk = \"2.8.0\"/hk = \"$V\"/" "$D/main/mise.toml"
    sed -i "s/v2\.8\.0/v$V/g; s/hk@2\.8\.0/hk@$V/g" "$D/main/hk.pkl"
    git -C "$D/main" commit -q -am "build(deps): pin hk $V in the scratch copy"
    git -C "$D/main" push -q origin main
  fi
  (cd "$D/main" && mise x -- hk --version && mise x -- hk install --mise) 2>&1

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# pin.sh <run dir>: which part of `git push` from a linked worktree writes core.worktree?
# Each experiment pushes a new branch from wt1 with one variable changed.
. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh
. "$R/lib.sh"
D=$1 W=$1/wt1
cp "$D/main/.git/config" "$D/config.snap"
exp() { # exp <name> <env assignments...> -- <command...>
  local name=$1; shift
  local envs=()
  while [ "$1" != -- ]; do envs+=("$1"); shift; done; shift
  git -C "$W" switch -q -c "pin-$name" 2>/dev/null || git -C "$W" switch -q "pin-$name"
  printf '\n%s\n' "$name" >> "$W/README.md"
  HK=0 git -C "$W" commit -qam "docs: pin $name"
  { echo "### $name: ${envs[*]} $*"; (cd "$W" && env "${envs[@]}" "$@"); echo "exit $?"; } >> "$D/pin.txt" 2>&1
  rec "$D" "pin $name: ${envs[*]} $*"
}
: > "$D/pin.txt"
exp hk0          HK=0 -- git push -q -u origin pin-hk0
exp nou          X=1 -- git push -q origin pin-nou
exp skipstep     HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests -- git push -q -u origin pin-skipstep
exp nolibgit2    HK_LIBGIT2=0 HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests -- git push -q -u origin pin-nolibgit2
exp byhand       HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests -- mise x -- hk run pre-push
exp byhand-args  HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests -- sh -c 'git rev-parse HEAD | sed "s|.*|refs/heads/x & refs/heads/x 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000|" | mise x -- hk run pre-push origin "$(git remote get-url origin)"'
exp check-from-ref X=1 -- mise x -- hk check --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD
exp fix-from-ref X=1 -- mise x -- hk fix --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD


```

**Output:**
```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# mechanism.sh <run dir>: the two halves of the write, each on its own.
#  1. git: `git init` run from a hook of a linked worktree (GIT_DIR inherited) re-initializes that worktree's
#     repository and guesses it is bare: core.bare = true in the shared config.
#  2. who then writes core.worktree: git itself, hk 2.8.0 or hk 2.11.0, with libgit2 or the git CLI backend.
. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh
. "$R/lib.sh"
D=$1 W=$1/wt1 G=$1/main/.git/worktrees/wt1 CFG=$1/main/.git/config
: > "$D/mechanism.txt"
bare() { git config --file "$CFG" --get core.bare; }
reset() { git config --file "$CFG" core.bare false; git config --file "$CFG" --unset core.worktree; cp "$CFG" "$D/config.snap"; }
log() { echo "### $*" >> "$D/mechanism.txt"; }

reset
mkdir -p "$D/elsewhere" && rm -rf "$D/elsewhere/.git"
log "GIT_DIR=<wt1 gitdir> git init -q (cwd: an unrelated directory, as test/helpers.ts sandbox() does)"
(cd "$D/elsewhere" && GIT_DIR=$G git init -q) >> "$D/mechanism.txt" 2>&1
rec "$D" "1. GIT_DIR=<wt1 gitdir> git init (cwd elsewhere): core.bare=$(bare)"
ls -a "$D/elsewhere" >> "$D/mechanism.txt"
log "same, then git commit --allow-empty (the second git call in sandbox())"
(cd "$D/elsewhere" && GIT_DIR=$G git -c user.name=test -c user.email=[redacted:email] commit -q --allow-empty -m init) >> "$D/mechanism.txt" 2>&1
echo "exit $?" >> "$D/mechanism.txt"
rec "$D" "1b. GIT_DIR=<wt1 gitdir> git commit --allow-empty: core.bare=$(bare)"

for cmd in "git status --short" "mise x hk@2.8.0 -- hk check" "mise x hk@2.11.0 -- hk check" \
  "env HK_LIBGIT2=0 mise x hk@2.11.0 -- hk check" "mise x hk@2.8.0 -- hk run pre-push" \
  "mise x hk@2.11.0 -- hk run pre-push"; do
  for how in plain hookenv; do
    reset; git config --file "$CFG" core.bare true; cp "$CFG" "$D/config.snap"
    if [ $how = hookenv ]; then pre="GIT_DIR=<wt1 gitdir> "; else pre=; fi
    log "core.bare=true, then in wt1: $pre$cmd"
    if [ $how = hookenv ]; then
      (cd "$W" && HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests GIT_DIR=$G $cmd) >> "$D/mechanism.txt" 2>&1
    else
      (cd "$W" && HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests $cmd) >> "$D/mechanism.txt" 2>&1
    fi
    echo "exit $?" >> "$D/mechanism.txt"
    rec "$D" "2. bare=true, wt1: $pre$cmd -> core.bare=$(bare)"
  done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# flip.sh <run dir>: replace the pre-push step by one that does what the unit tests do to the shared config
# (core.bare = true, through the inherited GIT_DIR), then push from wt1 and see who writes core.worktree.
. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh
. "$R/lib.sh"
D=$1 W=$1/wt1 CFG=$1/main/.git/config
: > "$D/flip.txt"
git config --file "$CFG" core.bare false; git config --file "$CFG" --unset core.worktree; cp "$CFG" "$D/config.snap"
git -C "$W" switch -q -c flip 2>/dev/null || git -C "$W" switch -q flip
# pre-push: one step that flips core.bare like `GIT_DIR=<wt gitdir> git init` does, and nothing else
perl -0pi -e 's/\["unit_tests"\] \{\n        check = "bun test test\/unit"/["unit_tests"] {\n        check = "git config core.bare true"/' "$W/hk.pkl"
grep -n 'core.bare' "$W/hk.pkl" >> "$D/flip.txt"
HK=0 git -C "$W" commit -qam "build: flip core.bare in pre-push"
try() { # try <label> <env...> -- push args
  local label=$1; shift; local envs=()
  while [ "$1" != -- ]; do envs+=("$1"); shift; done; shift
  printf '\n%s\n' "$label" >> "$W/README.md"; HK=0 git -C "$W" commit -qam "docs: $label"
  { echo "### $label: ${envs[*]} git push $*"; (cd "$W" && env "${envs[@]}" git push "$@"); echo "exit $?"; } >> "$D/flip.txt" 2>&1
  rec "$D" "flip $label: ${envs[*]} git push $* (bare=$(git config --file "$CFG" --get core.bare))"
  git config --file "$CFG" core.bare false; cp "$CFG" "$D/config.snap"
}
try hook X=1 -- -q -u origin flip
try hook-libgit2-off HK_LIBGIT2=0 -- -q origin flip
try hk0 HK=0 -- -q origin flip
git -C "$W" switch -q feat/wt1

# minimal-repro.sh <hk version>: self-contained. A pre-push step that runs `git init` in a temporary directory (as a
# test helper does) writes core.worktree into the shared config of the repository when the push comes from a linked

amends "package://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v$V/hk@$V#/Config.pkl"
hooks {
  ["pre-push"] {
    steps {
      // what a test suite does when it creates a scratch repository
      ["scratch_repo"] { check = "cd \"\$(mktemp -d)\" && git init -q" }
    }
  }
}
EOF

git push -q -u origin work 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -3
echo "after push:  core.worktree=$(git config --file "$D/main/.git/config" --get core.worktree || echo '<unset>')"
echo "git status in the main checkout now lists:"; git -C "$D/main" status --short | head -5

Bumps hk from 2.8.0 to 2.11.0: `mise.toml` and both `package://…/hk@X#/…` URLs in `hk.pkl`. Nothing else mentions the version.

The renovate regex manager for `hk.pkl` still matches both strings: checked with the regexes from `renovate.json` against the new file (`2.11.0` ×2 for each regex).

## Why

1. **Stash in linked worktrees.** 2.8.1 makes stashing separate for each linked worktree (jdx/hk#1746, #1747), and our workers commit in parallel from linked worktrees with `stash = "git"`.
2. **The `core.worktree` investigation.** That investigation (below) found that **hk is not what writes `core.worktree`**. This bump does not fix it; the fix belongs in `test/helpers.ts` and is proposed as a separate PR.

## Release notes that matter (2.8.1 → 2.11.0)

- **2.8.1:**
  - hk's stash entries leave the shared `refs/stash` and go to `refs/hk/stash/<commit>`, so `git stash list` no longer shows them;
  - the stash lock is per worktree, so hooks in different worktrees run in parallel.

  Before, a `git stash pop/drop/push` in one worktree could take hk's entry while a hook ran in another, and that hook then failed.
- **2.8.2:**
  - no more config-cache parse warnings when several hk processes start at once (parallel agents);
  - `hk check <file>` resolves paths from the current directory (we don't pass files).
- **2.9.0:** zsh files count as `shell` (we have no shell steps).
- **2.10.0:**
  - an optional hook-level `timeout` (not used here);
  - a clearer message for malformed pre-push stdin.
- **2.11.0:**
  - `stash = "git"` handles unstaged deletions;
  - the `tsc` builtin reports structured diagnostics.

No breaking change to `hk.pkl`, the builtins we use, or hook behaviour. `hk validate` passes.

## Verification

- `mise install`, then `mise x -- hk --version` in the worktree → `hk 2.11.0`.
- `mise x -- hk check --all --no-progress`, before (2.8.0) and after (2.11.0): the same 9 steps pass with byte-identical output. No new warnings; the only "warn" match is oxlint's `--deny-warnings` flag.
- `mise x -- hk run check --all` → exit 0.
- `mise x -- hk run pre-commit` on the staged bump: all steps pass, and "No unstaged changes to stash".
- `hk run commit-msg`:
  - `update stuff` is rejected (`Invalid commit type: 'update stuff'`, exit 1);
  - `build(deps): bump hk to 2.11.0` is accepted (exit 0).
- `mise run check`: lint, fmt:check, typecheck, 879 unit tests pass.
- **Hooks bypassed for this PR:** I committed and pushed with `HK=0 git commit` / `HK=0 git push`, as instructed, because the reproduction shows the pre-push hook is not safe in linked worktrees yet. I ran `mise run check` myself before pushing.
- **Main checkout after the push:** `git -C [redacted:repo] config --get core.worktree` is unset (exit 1). The shared `.git/config` mtime changed, from `git push -u` adding `[branch "build/hk-2.11"]`; that is git itself.

## Decision on `stash`

Keep `stash = "git"`. In the reproduction, 2.11.0:
- leaves no entry on the shared `refs/stash` during a hook;
- uses one `hk-stash.lock` per worktree (`.git/worktrees/<wt>/hk-stash.lock`);
- in 9 rounds of simultaneous commits from two worktrees, each with staged and unstaged changes, kept each worktree's unstaged change and only its own.

## Reproduction: who writes `core.worktree` (scratch repos under `/tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro`, isolated HOME/XDG/mise/hk state, local bare origin)

| Step (in linked worktree `wt1` unless noted) | HK=0 | hk 2.8.0 | hk 2.11.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git add` | no | no | no |
| `git commit`, staged only | no | no | no |
| `git commit`, staged + unstaged (hk stashes) | no | no | no |
| `git push -u origin <branch>` (pre-push runs `bun test test/unit`) | no | **yes** | **yes** |
| `git push` with `HK_SKIP_STEPS=unit_tests` (also with `HK_LIBGIT2=0`) | – | no | – |
| `hk run pre-commit` / `hk check` / `hk run commit-msg` / `hk run pre-push` by hand | no | no | no |
| commit and push from the main clone while worktrees exist | no | no | no |
| push with `sandbox()` dropping `GIT_*` from its environment | – | – | no |

| Stash | hk 2.8.0 | hk 2.11.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hk's entry on the shared `refs/stash` during the hook | yes (observed) | no |
| stash lock | one, in the common git dir (serializes all worktrees) | per worktree |
| unstaged changes lost or mixed, 9 simultaneous rounds | no | no |
| plain `git stash push` in wt2 while wt1's hook holds its stash | both kept | both kept |

I did not reproduce a loss with 2.8.0 (I tried `push` in the other worktree, not `pop`), but its entry does sit on the shared stack, which is the case 2.8.1 fixes.

### Mechanism

1. When the pre-push hook runs in a linked worktree, git exports `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git/worktrees/<wt>`. hk adds `GIT_WORK_TREE=<worktree root>` to its step commands when `GIT_DIR` is set; it does this on purpose in 2.8.0 and 2.11.0 (`src/step/runner.rs`).
2. The step runs `bun test test/unit`. `test/unit/helpers.test.ts` calls `sandbox()` in `test/helpers.ts`, which runs `git init` and `git commit --allow-empty -m init` with the inherited environment.
3. With both variables set, `git init` (cwd: the sandbox) re-initializes **the worker's** repository. Since the work tree is not the parent of `GIT_DIR`, it writes `core.worktree=<worktree>` into the shared `.git/config`. With `GIT_DIR` alone, it writes `core.bare=true` instead.
4. The following `git commit` also targets the worker's repository. It ran the worker's pre-commit hook on the worker's index, and only the commit-msg hook (rejecting `init`) prevented an empty commit on the worker's branch.
5. A main-checkout push is unaffected.

A 30-line self-contained reproduction, a pre-push step running `cd "$(mktemp -d)" && git init -q`, shows the same thing with 2.8.0 and 2.11.0, and `git status` in the main checkout then lists the worktree's changes. I filed no upstream issue: hk sets `GIT_WORK_TREE` on purpose, and git's own `GIT_DIR` already corrupts the shared config through the same `git init`.

## Risks

- If 2.11.0 behaved differently on a path the reproduction didn't cover (`hk fix`, file arguments), the hooks would show it at the next commit. CI's `hk check --all` runs the same version from `mise.toml`.
- Until the `test/helpers.ts` fix lands, pushing from a linked worktree with hooks can still set `core.worktree` (or `core.bare=true`) in the main checkout's shared config, whatever the hk version.

# real checkouts (SRC is only read: `git fetch` from it).
mode=${1:?before|after}
. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh # isolated HOME, XDG, mise and hk state; unsets GIT_*, HK_*, MISE_*
. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/lib.sh # rec
unset HK                            # the hook command is `test "${HK:-1}" = "0" || mise x -- hk run <hook> --from-hook`
SRC=[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-testenv
MODULES=$SRC/node_modules
D=$R/testenv-$mode
OUT=/tmp/opencode/rog/testenv
log=$OUT/e2e-$mode.txt
: > "$log"
say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$log"; }

# like lib.sh's setup, without pinning hk: origin/main already uses the version under test
rm -rf "$D"
mkdir -p "$D"
git init -q --bare "$D/origin.git"
git -C "$D/origin.git" fetch -q "$SRC" refs/remotes/origin/main:refs/heads/main
git -C "$D/origin.git" symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main
git clone -q "$D/origin.git" "$D/main"
echo node_modules >> "$D/main/.git/info/exclude"
ln -s "$MODULES" "$D/main/node_modules"
(cd "$D/main" && mise x -- hk --version && mise x -- hk install --mise) 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
git -C "$D/main" worktree add -q -b feat/wt1 "$D/wt1" main
ln -s "$MODULES" "$D/wt1/node_modules"
cp "$D/main/.git/config" "$D/config.snap"

cfg=$D/main/.git/config
snap() {
  local status lines
  if status=$(git -C "$D/main" status --porcelain 2>&1); then lines=$(printf '%s' "$status" | grep -c .)
  else lines="error: ${status%%$'\n'*}"; fi
  printf '%-28s core.bare=%-5s core.worktree=%-32s config-sha256=%s main-status-lines=%s feat/wt1=%s\n' "$1" \
    "$(git config --file "$cfg" --get core.bare)" "$(git config --file "$cfg" --get core.worktree || echo '<unset>')" \
    "$(sha256sum "$cfg" | cut -c1-12)" "$lines" "$(git -C "$D/main" rev-parse --short feat/wt1)" | tee -a "$log"
}

say "== mode: $mode   git: $(git --version)   hook entries: $(git config --file "$cfg" --get-regexp '^hook\.' | wc -l)"
say "origin/main: $(git -C "$D/main" log --oneline -1 main)"
if [ "$mode" = after ]; then
  git -C "$D/wt1" fetch -q "$SRC" refs/heads/fix/test-git-env
  git -C "$D/wt1" merge -q --ff-only FETCH_HEAD
fi
say "wt1 HEAD: $(git -C "$D/wt1" log --oneline -1)"
say "wt1 test/helpers.ts has childEnv(): $(grep -c 'export function childEnv' "$D/wt1/test/helpers.ts")"
snap "after setup"

# a commit with the hooks (pre-commit, commit-msg), then a push (pre-push: bun test test/unit), from the linked worktree
git -C "$D/wt1" commit -q --allow-empty -m "test: trigger the hooks" > "$OUT/commit-$mode.txt" 2>&1
say "commit exit=$?"
snap "after commit in wt1"
cp "$cfg" "$D/config.before-push"
git -C "$D/wt1" push origin feat/wt1 > "$OUT/push-$mode.txt" 2>&1
say "push exit=$?   origin feat/wt1: $(git -C "$D/origin.git" rev-parse --short feat/wt1 2>&1)"
grep -E 'unit_tests|[0-9]+ (pass|fail)' "$OUT/push-$mode.txt" | tail -n 5 | tee -a "$log"
snap "after push from wt1"
say "--- diff of the shared .git/config across the push (empty = unchanged):"

1:# End-to-end check for fix/test-git-env: a push from a linked worktree with the hooks ACTIVE, without and with the fix.
2:# Usage: bash /tmp/opencode/rog/testenv/e2e.sh before|after
3:# Scratch only: a bare origin, a main clone and a linked worktree under $R/testenv-<mode>; nothing here touches the
6:. /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/env.sh # isolated HOME, XDG, mise and hk state; unsets GIT_*, HK_*, MISE_*
9:SRC=[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-testenv
11:D=$R/testenv-$mode
12:OUT=/tmp/opencode/rog/testenv
18:rm -rf "$D"
44:  git -C "$D/wt1" fetch -q "$SRC" refs/heads/fix/test-git-env

```

{"additions":106,"changedFiles":4,"commits":["test(helpers): keep the hook's git environment out of sandbox()","test(integration): keep the hook's git environment away from npm","docs(agents): explain why tests that start git must drop GIT_*"],"deletions":18,"title":"fix(test): keep the hook's git environment out of sandbox()"}
--- body:
Fixes the cause of the `core.worktree` / `core.bare=true` writes in the main checkout's shared `.git/config`, found in the hk investigation (#9, "Mechanism").

## Cause

When the pre-push hook runs in a linked worktree, git exports `GIT_DIR=<main>/.git/worktrees/<wt>`, and hk adds `GIT_WORK_TREE=<worktree root>` to its step commands (on purpose). The step runs `bun test test/unit`. `sandbox()` in `test/helpers.ts` then ran `git init` and `git commit --allow-empty -m init` in its temporary project **with the inherited environment**, so git acted on the worker's repository:

- with both variables, `git init` wrote `core.worktree=<worktree>` into the shared `.git/config`;
- with `GIT_DIR` alone, it wrote `core.bare=true`;
- `git commit` committed on the worker's branch. In the real repository only the commit-msg hook (which rejects `init`) stopped it. The new test shows the stray commit (`refs/heads/feature` moves).

## Changes

- `test/helpers.ts`: a new exported `childEnv()` returns the caller's environment without `GIT_*` and `HERDR_*`. The existing herdr filter from 649dc6d moves into it, so there is one mechanism with one comment explaining each prefix.
  - `sandbox()` builds its `env` from `childEnv()` plus its own overrides (`PWD`, `READONLY_GUARD_*`, `XDG_*`, and `HERDR_*` when `herdr: true`), and now passes that `env` to `git init` and `git commit` as well as to opencode.
  - `hasOpencode` uses `childEnv()` too.
  - The sandbox sets no `GIT_*` variable of its own; there was none to keep.
- `test/unit/helpers.test.ts` (written first; it fails on main): two cases, `GIT_DIR` alone and `GIT_DIR` + `GIT_WORK_TREE`.
  - Setup: a scratch repository with a linked worktree, the variables pointed at it in `process.env`, then `sandbox()`.
  - Asserts that the scratch repo's config is byte-identical (including `core.bare` / `core.worktree`), that both HEADs and all refs are unchanged, that `box.env` has no `GIT_*`, and that the sandbox is a repository of its own with only its `init` commit.
  - `afterEach` restores `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` and the `HERDR_*` variables.
  - The fixture's own `git()` strips `GIT_*` itself, independently of `childEnv()`. That keeps the test safe inside a hook even if `childEnv()` regressed.
- `test/integration/package.test.ts`: `sh()` (`npm pack`, `npm install` in a temporary directory, `tar`) uses `childEnv()`, because npm may run git.
- `AGENTS.md`: a "Tests run inside git hooks" hazard, and `childEnv()` added to the map entry for `helpers.ts`.

Not changed, on purpose:
- `hk.pkl`, `mise.toml` and the hook commands: no defense in depth in this PR.
- No CHANGELOG entry: this is test infrastructure.

## Other places checked

- **`test/`:**
  - `child_process` is used only in `test/helpers.ts` and `test/integration/package.test.ts`.
  - `opencode.test.ts`, `copies.test.ts` and the e2e test start processes only through `sandbox()` (`box.opencode()`, and `registeredToolIds()`, which uses `box.env`).
  - The installed-CLI calls in `package.test.ts` (`check`, `--version`, `rules`) run no git, so they are left as they are.
- **`src/`:** nothing runs git. The only child process is `systemIo().run` in `src/commands.ts`. It starts `opencode plugin …` for the `install` subcommand with the user's own environment, which is correct, so it is unchanged.

## Verification

**The new test on unfixed `test/helpers.ts`** fails in both cases:

```
GIT_DIR:                    core: "core.bare false" -> "core.bare true";  refs/heads/feature 5200196 -> 12bcd10 (stray commit)
GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE:  config gains "worktree = /tmp/rg-hook-…/worktree";  refs/heads/feature 5200196 -> 12bcd10
(fail) a hook's GIT_DIR does not take the sandbox's git to the caller's repository
(fail) a hook's GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE does not take the sandbox's git to the caller's repository
 3 pass / 2 fail
```

With the fix: 5 pass, 0 fail.

**End to end, hooks ACTIVE**, in scratch repos under `/tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/testenv-{before,after}`:
- Isolation: `env.sh` (HOME, XDG, mise and hk state; `GIT_*`/`HK_*`/`MISE_*` unset, `HK` unset).
- `rec` from `lib.sh`.
- git 2.55 with config-based hooks installed by `hk install --mise`, hk 2.11.0 as on main.
- A local bare origin, a main clone, and a linked worktree `wt1`.
- Steps in `wt1`: an empty commit with the hooks, then `git push origin feat/wt1`. The pre-push hook runs `bun test test/unit`.
- The push is made without `-u`, so git itself does not write the config.
- Script: `/tmp/opencode/rog/testenv/e2e.sh before|after`.
  - *before*: `wt1` is at origin/main b14eef3.
  - *after*: `wt1` is fast-forwarded to this branch.

Before (origin/main, no fix):
```
after setup                  core.bare=false core.worktree=<unset>   config-sha256=8cd04c1656e8 feat/wt1=b14eef3
after commit in wt1          core.bare=false core.worktree=<unset>   config-sha256=8cd04c1656e8 feat/wt1=2b27263
push exit=0   ✔ unit_tests (879 pass, 0 fail)
after push from wt1          core.bare=false core.worktree=/tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/testenv-before/wt1 config-sha256=4f9083079b37
--- diff of the shared .git/config across the push:
> 	worktree = /tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/testenv-before/wt1
lib.sh rec: push from wt1 (before)   core.worktree=/tmp/opencode/rog/hk-repro/testenv-before/wt1 config-changed=yes

```

## Hooks bypassed for this PR

The pre-push hook is exactly what this PR fixes, so until it is merged I committed and pushed with `HK=0 git commit` / `HK=0 git push`. I followed Conventional Commits by hand and ran `mise run check` myself before pushing.

## Assistant (Build · Claude Sonnet 5.5 · 53.3s)

_Thinking:_
I've got PR #10 ready with CI green, so the next step is asking the user to merge. While they decide, I can prepare the rog-deploy brief and send a notification. I'm weighing whether to pair the notice with a question through the Question tool, then run the deploy once they confirm the merge.

I'm going to write the deploy as a deterministic script instead of having the throwaway session improvise. The agent will run that script and report back, which keeps the procedure repeatable and the worker's context small.

I'm weighing whether the deploy should abort and report if `core.worktree` is set, or unset it since the root cause is fixed. The steps after that are to fetch origin, check HEAD and the incoming commits, back up `dist`, and pull fast-forward only.

I'm weighing a scratch clone of origin/main for the build and test, then swapping the built dist into the main checkout, since that keeps the tests independent of whatever dist currently sits there.

I'm checking whether the build can go into a scratch copy at the target commit and then swap into main, which would make the outage far shorter than rebuilding in place. The open question is whether a dist built from a different path comes out identical.

I'm writing the spot-check list now: a handful of commands with their expected verdicts, such as a sort with `-o` that should block and a plain pipeline that should allow. I'm also checking the export-with-diff case against the verdict from PR #7.

I'm listing the last spot-check expectations, the hk version pin, and a check that `core.worktree` is unset afterward, then I'll set up a rollback in case anything fails after the swap.

I'm planning a dry-run mode for the deploy script that does the build and integration tests in scratch space without pulling or swapping anything. I'm also holding off on running the full build myself, since it's CPU-heavy and takes several minutes.

I'm settling on the agent running the deploy script in one approved command, which covers the write to main as the one exception I'm signing off on. The integration tests are heavy since they spin up opencode sandboxes, but that's acceptable for this rollout.

Next I'll write the deploy script, then send the merge question with "deploy ready" in the same message, since the user will be deciding anyway.


_Thinking:_
PR #10 is green and waiting on you, so I'm turning the deploy procedure into a tested script that builds in a scratch clone and swaps `dist/` in with two renames, so sessions never see a missing plugin.


**Tool: write**

**Input:**
```json
{
  "filePath": "/tmp/opencode/rog/bin/deploy-main.sh",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# deploy-main.sh [--dry-run] [--skip-integration]\n# Update the main checkout of opencode-readonly-guard and its dist/, which every opencode session of the fleet loads\n# (file://[redacted:repo]). Procedure:\n#   1. preflight on the main checkout: clean tree, on main, core.worktree/core.bare sane\n#   2. fetch; build + test the target commit in a SCRATCH clone (never in main), so tests cannot disturb the fleet\n#   3. spot-check the freshly built CLI against expected verdicts\n#   4. only then: git pull --ff-only in main and swap dist/ with two renames (the plugin is missing for ~1 ms)\n#   5. verify the live dist/ again; on any failure restore the previous dist/ (git is never rewound)\n# --dry-run: do 1-3 only. --skip-integration: skip `mise run test:integration` (unit tests + spot-checks still run).\n# Output: one block of KEY=value lines at the end, status OK | FAILED_BEFORE_SWAP | ROLLED_BACK.\n# Never prints the environment (it holds secrets).\nset -uo pipefail\n\nMAIN=[redacted:repo]\nWORK=/tmp/opencode/rog/deploy\nTS=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)\ndry=0 skip_int=0\nfor a in \"$@\"; do\n  case $a in\n    --dry-run) dry=1 ;;\n    --skip-integration) skip_int=1 ;;\n    *) echo \"usage: $0 [--dry-run] [--skip-integration]\" >&2; exit 64 ;;\n  esac\ndone\n# a hook or a tool may have exported these; nothing here may act on another repository\nfor v in $(env | cut -d= -f1 | grep -E '^GIT_'); do unset \"$v\"; done\n\nstatus=FAILED_BEFORE_SWAP\ndeclare -a SUMMARY=()\nnote() { printf '%s\\n' \"$*\"; }\nkv() { SUMMARY+=(\"$1=$2\"); }\nfinish() {\n  echo; echo \"===== deploy summary =====\"\n  printf 'STATUS=%s\\n' \"$status\"\n  printf '%s\\n' \"${SUMMARY[@]}\"\n  [ \"$status\" = OK ] || [ \"$dry\" = 1 -a \"$status\" = DRY_RUN_OK ]\n}\nfail() { note \"FAIL: $*\"; kv FAILED_AT \"$*\"; finish; exit 1; }\nmg() { git -C \"$MAIN\" \"$@\"; }\n\n# ---- 1. preflight -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\nnote \"== preflight\"\n[ \"$(mg rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)\" = main ] || fail \"main checkout is not on branch main\"\n[ -z \"$(mg status --porcelain)\" ] || fail \"main checkout has uncommitted changes: $(mg status --porcelain | head -5 | tr '\\n' ';')\"\nif mg config --get core.worktree >/dev/null 2>&1; then fail \"core.worktree is set in main's .git/config (known corruption signature): report to rog-orch, do not unset\"; fi\n[ \"$(mg config --get core.bare)\" = false ] || fail \"core.bare is not false\"\nOLD_SHA=$(mg rev-parse --short HEAD)\nmg fetch -q origin || fail \"git fetch failed\"\nNEW_SHA=$(mg rev-parse --short origin/main)\nkv OLD_SHA \"$OLD_SHA\"; kv NEW_SHA \"$NEW_SHA\"\nINCOMING=$(mg log --oneline HEAD..origin/main | wc -l)\nkv INCOMING_COMMITS \"$INCOMING\"\nmg log --oneline HEAD..origin/main | head -40 | sed 's/^/  incoming: /'\nif [ \"$INCOMING\" = 0 ] && [ \"$dry\" = 0 ]; then status=OK; kv NOTE \"already up to date; dist/ untouched\"; finish; exit 0; fi\nmg merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main || fail \"local main has diverged from origin/main (not a fast-forward)\"\n\n# ---- 2. build + test the target in a scratch clone ----------------------------------------------------------------\nnote \"== scratch build of $NEW_SHA\"\nrm -rf \"$WORK\"; do\n    want=${item%%|*} cmd=${item#*|}\n    node \"$cli\" check --no-store \"$cmd\" >/dev/null 2>&1; code=$?\n    case $code in 0) got=allow ;; 1) got=ask ;; 2) got=block ;; *) got=\"exit$code\" ;; esac\n    if [ \"$got\" != \"$want\" ]; // Start `opencode serve` in the current (sandbox) project, subscribe to the event streams the way a client would,
// and report which toasts arrive. Mode "event": the first request is the /event subscription (it boots the instance).
// Mode "global": subscribe to /global/event first, then boot the instance with GET /config.
import { spawn } from "node:child_process"

const mode = process.argv[2] ?? "event"
const project = process.cwd()
const child = spawn("opencode", ["serve", "--port", "0", "--hostname", "127.0.0.1"], {
  env: process.env,
  stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
})
let output = ""
const url = await new Promise<string>((resolve, reject) => {
  const read = (chunk: Buffer) => {
    output += chunk.toString()
    const address = /listening on (http:\/\/\S+)/.exec(output)?.[1]
    if (address) resolve(address)
  }
  child.stdout.on("data", read)
  child.stderr.on("data", read)
  child.on("exit", (status) => reject(new Error(`serve exited ${status}: ${output}`)))
})

const seen: string[] = []
async function listen(path: string) {
  const response = await fetch(`${url}${path}`, { headers: { "x-opencode-directory": project } })
  const reader = response.body!.getReader()
  const decoder = new TextDecoder()
  let buffer = ""
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read()
    if (done) return
    buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
    for (const line of buffer.split("\n").slice(0, -1)) {
      if (!line.startsWith("data:")) continue
      const data = JSON.parse(line.slice(5)) as { type?: string; payload?: { type?: string; properties?: unknown } }
      const type = data.type ?? data.payload?.type
      const props = (data as { properties?: { message?: string } }).properties ?? data.payload?.properties
      seen.push(`${path} ${type}${type?.includes("toast") ? ` ${JSON.stringify(props)}` : ""}`)
    }
    buffer = buffer.slice(buffer.lastIndexOf("\n") + 1)
  }
}

if (mode === "event") void listen("/event")
else {
  void listen("/global/event")
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1500))
  const config = await fetch(`${url}/config`, { headers: { "x-opencode-directory": project } })
  seen.push(`GET /config ${config.status}`)
}
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 8000))
console.log(seen.join("\n"))
child.kill("SIGTERM")
process.exit(0)
/tmp/opencode/rog/doctor/toast-exp.ts:9:  env: process.env,

#!/bin/bash
# Which ps command lines show process environments? Starts one sleep whose environment holds only a marker, then
# runs each case and prints how many output lines contain the marker. It prints counts only, never an environment.
set -u
pid=$(bun -e 'const p = Bun.spawn(["/usr/bin/sleep", "60"], { env: { MARKER_ZZ: "1" }, stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "ignore"] }); p.unref(); console.log(p.pid)')
trap 'kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
P=$pid
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [ -z "$line" ] && continue
  args=${line//PID/$P}
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  count=$(ps $args 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'MARKER_Z[Z]=1')
  printf '%-45s %s\n' "$line" "$count"
done <<'EOF'
e -p PID -o pid,args
-p PID -o pid,args
-p PID -o pid,environ
-p PID -o environ:20
-p PID -o pid,args e
-p PID e
eww -p PID
axe
aux
-ef
-ef -o pid,args
-e -o pid,args
-eo pid,args
-f -e -o pid,args
-ef -u x
-e -u x
-eu x
-e -g x
-e -s x
-ef -t
-e -t zz
-p PID -e -o pid,args --sort=pid
o pid,etime,args -p PID
-o pid,etime,args -p PID
p PID o pid,args
p PID -o pid,args -u x
-p PID -u x
-e --user x
EOF

```

#!/bin/bash
# Which combinations of ps -e with other SysV/GNU options show environments (through the BSD second-chance parse)?
# Starts one sleep whose environment holds only a marker; prints the combinations whose output shows the marker.
# Prints command lines and counts only, never an environment.
set -u
pid=$(bun -e 'const p = Bun.spawn(["/usr/bin/sleep", "120"], { env: { MARKER_ZZ: "1" }, stdio: ["ignore", "ignore", "ignore"] }); p.unref(); console.log(p.pid)')
trap 'kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
ewords=(-e -ef -eF -el -elf -ely -ej -ejH -eH -ew -eww -efww -eLf -eT -eM -eZ -ec -eN -ed -ea -eA -ex -er -eS -eu -eg -es -et -eU -eG -eC)
extras=("" -f -F -l -y -j -H -w -L -T -m -c -M -Z -a -A -d -N -x -r "-u x" "-t" "-g x" "-s x" "-U x" "-G x" "-C x" "-p $pid" "-q $pid")
formats=("" "-o pid,args" "-O args" "-o args=CMD")
gnus=("" --forest "--sort=pid" --no-headers "--cols 200" "--width 200" "--format pid,args" "--ppid 1" "--pid $pid" "--headers" "--cumulative" "--deselect" "--user x" "--tty x")
total=0
leaks=0
for e in "${ewords[@]}"; do
  for x in "${extras[@]}"; do
    for f in "${formats[@]}"; do
      for g in "${gnus[@]}"; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        count=$(ps $e $x $f $g 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'MARKER_Z[Z]=1')
        total=$((total + 1))
        if [ "$count" != 0 ]; then
          leaks=$((leaks + 1))
          echo "LEAK: ps $e $x $f $g" | sed "s/$pid/PID/g"
        fi
      done
    done
  done
done
echo "combinations: $total, showing the environment: $leaks"
23:          echo "LEAK: ps $e $x $f $g" | sed "s/$pid/PID/g"
29:echo "combinations: $total, showing the environment: $leaks"

```

## Why

When the plugin fails to start, opencode does not stop: `plan` and `explore` silently keep its defaults, `bash: * allow` with no write guard.

| Failure | What opencode 1.19.3 does |
| --- | --- |
| the file cannot be imported (no `dist/`, a `file://` path that does not exist) | nothing on stderr, `opencode debug config` exits 0 and still lists the entry |
| `server()` throws (a corrupt `rules/allow.json`) | one `failed to load plugin` line in opencode's log, plugin dropped |
| the `config` hook throws | `plugin config hook failed` in opencode's log, startup continues |

## What changes

**Fail closed** (`plugin.ts`, `copies.ts`, `inject.ts`, `rules.ts`)
- The rule files are loaded one by one, as approved in the amendment: the write guard only needs `commands.json`.
- If any of them cannot be read, the copy no longer throws. Unless a copy that started is in charge:
  - read-only agents ask before every command (`{"*": "ask", ...their own deny rules}`); a fully denied bash stays denied;
  - the review tools stay hidden and plan's subagent limits stay;
  - no review tools are registered and `/guard-review` is not added;
  - the write guard **stays on unless `commands.json` itself is broken**;
  - one `error` event is logged `{where: "load", error, writeGuard, roAgents, module}`;
  - one toast is shown: the reason, "the write guard is OFF" when that is the case, and "run `opencode-readonly-guard doctor`".
- An error inside the config hook: the same policy, `where: "config"`, with the write guard on.
- Several copies in one instance:
  - A copy that started, loaded before or after the broken one, is in charge. Its `init` event gains `failed: [{module, error}]`.
  - Among failed copies, the last one that still has a write guard acts, so only one event and one toast are produced.

```

#!/bin/bash
# Does `<program> <version flag>` write anything into an empty HOME? Prints the files each one creates.
set -u
check() {
  local home
  home=$(mktemp -d /tmp/opencode/rog/utilities/vhome.XXXXXX)
  HOME=$home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$home/.config XDG_CACHE_HOME=$home/.cache XDG_DATA_HOME=$home/.local/share \
    XDG_STATE_HOME=$home/.local/state timeout 20 "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local status=$?
  local files
  files=$(cd "$home" && find . -mindepth 1 | sort | tr '\n' ' ')
  printf '%-32s exit %-3s writes: %s\n' "$*" "$status" "${files:-nothing}"
  rm -rf "$home"
}
check bash --version
check "$(mise which tree-sitter)" --version
check tree-sitter --version

// Cost of the rule list: rules per read-only agent, time to build it, and time per stage for evaluate()/decide().
// Usage: bun bench.ts <checkout>   (imports the checkout's src/, nothing is built)
const root = process.argv[2]
const { buildBashRules, loadRules } = await import(`${root}/src/rules.ts`)
const { evaluate } = await import(`${root}/src/wildcard.ts`)
const { decide } = await import(`${root}/src/decide.ts`)

const rules = loadRules()
const time = (runs: number, run: () => void): number => {
  run()
  const start = performance.now()
  for (let i = 0; i < runs; i++) run()
  return (performance.now() - start) / runs
}
const bash = buildBashRules(rules)
const stages = [
  "git status",
  "ls -la src",
  "herdr --help 2>&1",
  "sed -n 1,5p f",
  "python3 -c 'print(1)'",
  "node --version",
  "rg -n foo src | head -20",
  "unknown-tool --flag",
]
const build = time(20, () => buildBashRules(rules))
const perEvaluate = time(200, () => stages.forEach((stage) => evaluate(stage, bash))) / stages.length
const perDecide = time(200, () => stages.forEach((stage) => decide(stage, bash))) / stages.length
const json = JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries(bash))
console.log(
  JSON.stringify({
    rules: bash.length,
    permissionJsonBytes: json.length,
    buildMs: +build.toFixed(2),
    evaluateMsPerStage: +perEvaluate.toFixed(3),
    decideMsPerStage: +perDecide.toFixed(3),
  }),
)

```

**Output:**
```
// What opencode would prompt for: one pattern per tree-sitter `command` node (the parent redirected_statement's text
// if any), cd/chdir/pushd/popd skipped. Compared with the repository's simpleCommands().
// Usage: bun probe.ts <checkout>
import { Language, Parser } from "web-tree-sitter"

const root = process.argv[2]
const { simpleCommands } = await import(`${root}/src/shell.ts`)
await Parser.init()
const parser = new Parser()
parser.setLanguage(await Language.load(new URL("node_modules/tree-sitter-bash/tree-sitter-bash.wasm", import.meta.url).pathname))

const SKIPPED = new Set(["cd", "chdir", "pushd", "popd"])
function opencode(src: string): string[] {
  const tree = parser.parse(src)
  if (!tree) return ["<no tree>"]
  const out: string[] = []
  for (const node of tree.rootNode.descendantsOfType("command")) {
    if (!node) continue
    const name = node.childForFieldName("name")?.text ?? ""
    if (SKIPPED.has(name)) continue
    const host = node.parent?.type === "redirected_statement" ? node.parent : node
    out.push(host.text)
  }
  return out
}
// Our text drops redirections and quotes; compare the first two words, which is what decides the rule family.
const key = (text: string) =>
  text
    .replace(/\s+\d*(>>?|<|&>)\s*\S+/g, "")
    .replace(/["']/g, "")

```

#!/bin/bash
# Can options before the subcommand make `git reflog` expire, delete, write or drop? Scratch repository only.
set -u
unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/opencode/rog/utilities/reflog.XXXXXX)
cd "$d" || exit 1
git init -q
for i in 1 2 3; do git -c user.name=t -c user.email=[redacted:email] commit -q --allow-empty -m "c$i"; done
count() { git reflog | wc -l; }
echo "start: $(count) entries"
for args in "-5 expire --expire=now --all" "-n 2 delete HEAD@{0}" "--date=iso drop --all" "-5 --date=iso HEAD" \
  "-1 write refs/heads/main $(git rev-parse HEAD) $(git rev-parse HEAD~1) msg" "--all expire --expire=now"; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  out=$(git reflog $args 2>&1 | head -1)
  echo "git reflog $args -> $(count) entries; first line: ${out:0:60}"
done
rm -rf "$d"

```

// Probe: does POST /session work in a checkout whose own plugin entry has no dist/?
import { rmSync } from "node:fs"
import { join } from "node:path"
import { copyPlugin, sandbox, withServer } from "[redacted:worktrees_root]/rog-doctor/test/helpers.ts"

const box = sandbox({ plugin: "." })
try {
  copyPlugin(box.project)
  rmSync(join(box.project, "dist"), { recursive: true })
  const result = await withServer(box, async (url) => {
    const headers = { "x-opencode-directory": box.project, "content-type": "application/json" }
    const created = await fetch(`${url}/session`, { method: "POST", headers, body: "{}" })
    const session = (await created.json()) as { id?: string; directory?: string }
    const listed = await fetch(`${url}/session`, { headers })
    return { status: created.status, session, listed: listed.status, count: ((await listed.json()) as unknown[]).length }
  })
  console.log(JSON.stringify(result))
  console.log("events", JSON.stringify(box.events()))
} finally {
  box.cleanup()
}

```

<skill_content name="opencode-sessions">
# Skill: opencode-sessions

# OpenCode Session Manager

Access and manage your OpenCode conversation history, switch between sessions, and export transcripts.

## Quick Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `/sessions` or `/resume` | List all past sessions |
| `/resume <session-id>` | Switch to a specific session |
| `/export` | Export current session to markdown |

## Storage Location

OpenCode stores conversation history in a **SQLite database**:

```
~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
```

This is a single database file (typically 1-2 GB) containing:
- All conversation messages
- Session metadata
- Tool outputs and results

**Other relevant directories:**
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `~/.local/share/opencode/log/` | Log files (last 10 sessions) |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/` | Session snapshots |
| `~/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/` | Tool execution outputs |
| `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | Configuration file |

## Usage

### List All Sessions

```
/sessions
```

Shows a numbered list of recent sessions with:
- Session ID
- Date/time started
- Brief preview of first message

### Resume a Session

```
/resume 3
```

Switches to session #3 from the list. Your current context changes to that session's state.

**Tip:** You can also use `/resume` without a number to see the interactive list.

### Export Transcript

```
/export
```

Exports the current session transcript to markdown format for easier reading, sharing, or archiving.

**Output location:** Usually saved to your working directory or a default exports folder.

### Export Specific Session

```
/export <session-id>
```

Export a different session by specifying its ID.

## Workflow Examples

### Finding a Previous Solution

```
User: /sessions

OpenCode: 
1. 2026-04-03 10:15 - "Help me debug Python script"
2. 2026-04-03 14:22 - "Create React component"
3. 2026-04-04 09:00 - "Explain Git workflows"

User: /resume 2

OpenCode: [Switches to session about React component]
```

### Archiving Important Conversations

```
User: /export

OpenCode: Session exported to session_20260404_120000.md

User: [Move the file to your notes folder]
```

### Continuing Long-Term Work

```
User: /sessions

[Find the session from last week about the architecture design]

User: /resume 5

[Continue the architecture discussion with full context preserved]
```

## Best Practices

1. **Name your sessions implicitly** — The first message often becomes the session identifier. Start with a clear description like "Architecture review for authentication system"

2. **Export before closing** — If a session has valuable information, `/export` it before starting a new topic

3. **Resume for context** — Switching sessions preserves the full conversation state, including file changes and tool outputs

4. **Database maintenance** — The `opencode.db` file grows over time. If it gets too large, you can:
   - Export important sessions to markdown for archiving
   - Use `/sessions` and `/export` to selectively save what matters

## Troubleshooting

### Session not found
- Check `/sessions` to see available session IDs
- Sessions may be cleared if the database was reset

### Export fails
- Ensure you have write permissions in the target directory
- Try specifying a full path: `/export /path/to/output.md`

### Database issues
- If `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is corrupted, OpenCode may create a new one
- Check `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot/` for recent session backups

---

**Related:** Use `/core-reflect` at session end to capture learnings from important conversations.

# [redacted:repo]

> Le [redacted:repo] de Silopolis: the basin where vessels are laid down and refitted.
> Part of the Silopolis workshop: libre, open, portable information systems.

[redacted:repo] is L1 in the Silopolis ecosystem (`[redacted:repo]:spec/drs/DR-001-four_layer_ecosystem_model.md`): the project factory.
It ships scaffolding templates, toolchain pins, quality gates and CI adapters that any project can be laid down from, and later refitted with (`radoub`, Phase B), via Copier.

## What lives here

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `spec/`, `spec/drs/`, `spec/contracts/` | [redacted:repo]'s own decision records and contracts, indexed per-directory (`DR-021`); entry point `spec/README.md` |
| `project/milestones/`, `project/tasks/` | [redacted:repo]'s own milestone and task records (`DR-017`/`DR-018`/`DR-021` branch, milestone and index model); entry point `project/roadmap.md` |
| `project/TODO.md`, `project/roadmap.md` | [redacted:repo]'s own piloting files: day-to-day kanban and structural sequencing (`DR-021`) |
| `docs/` | [redacted:repo]'s own documentation site, Diataxis-structured, Quarto-published (`DR-020`); `mise run docs:build` |
| `copier.yml` | the Copier entrypoint, at this repo's own root (`CT-001.R01`/`R05`, `_subdirectory: template`): what makes this repo a git-tracked Copier template a consumer can `copier copy` *and* `copier update` (`T-030`) |
| `template/` | the Copier template source, addressed via `_subdirectory`: `core`/`runtime`/`quality` module fragments (`template/copier/`) with real content, shared includes (`template/includes/`) (`CT-002`, `CT-004`; `T-002`/`T-003`) |
| `tests/` | the update round-trip harness (`mise run test:roundtrip`, `CT-003.R01`-`R04`/`R05` plus two doctrine checks), asserted against a real, throwaway-tagged Copier round trip of the whole repo, never [redacted:repo]'s own working tree, green since `T-003` |

What does **not** live here: domain content, lab material, or anything specific to a generated project.
Domain flavor enters only through optional template modules, never base assumptions (`DR-005`).

# Settings only: no private term may be written here. The terms live in the private store,

## Redaction

`scripts/session_redact.py` rewrites each export, in this order:

01. secrets (API keys, GitHub tokens, age secret keys, private key blocks) become `[redacted:secret]`;
01. `/home/<user>` becomes `~`; `/home/linuxbrew` (Homebrew's prefix on Linux) and the placeholder `/home/user` are not home directories and stay as they are;
01. identity values become `[redacted:user_<category>]`, where the rule applies (see below);
01. private terms become `[redacted:private]`; they come from the private store, never from this repository: the private spell lists, lists of extra terms, and a pattern for sentences quoted from the user's documents;
01. path aliases (`[redacted:worktrees_root]` becomes `[redacted:worktrees_root]`), where the rule applies;
01. `~/Work/<fleet repo>/<path>` becomes `` `<repo>:<path>` `` ([redacted:repo] `DR-012`); the public profile adds GitHub slugs, repository names and generic rules (below).

`python3 scripts/session_redact.py --check` must exit 0; it checks `memory/sessions/*.md` (the `check` setting of this repository's project file).
It prints counts per category and never prints the terms.


### Configuration layers

The store (`~/.local/share/[redacted:private]`, or `SESSION_REDACT_STORE`) is a git clone of a private GitHub repository, not of this one; its spell lists are also the private tier of the Neovim spell words (README, "Spell checking and word lists").
Settings and lists are read in layers; for a single setting the later layer wins, and every list is the union of the layers (a layer can add a term and cannot remove one):

| Layer | Where | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| global | `<store>/session-redact/` | the user's lists for every project, and an optional `config.toml` |
| project file | `.session-redact.toml` at the git root, committed | settings only, never a term |
| project directory | `<store>/<terms>/`, named by the project file | the project's own lists |
| terms-dir | `SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR` | one more lists directory: the command line of earlier consumers |
| option | `--profile` | the profile |

With no global directory, no project file and no `SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR`, the project directory is `<store>/nvim`.
The script exits with status 2, redacting nothing, when no layer exists, when a named directory is missing or when a configuration file is invalid; an unknown key in a configuration file is counted, never named.

The project file accepts `profile`, `terms` (the name of one directory of the store), `fleet-names`, `identity`, `path-aliases`, `check` and `exclude` (globs, relative to the file).
The global `config.toml` accepts `profile`, `fleet-names`, `identity`, `path-aliases` and `spell` (directories of `*.add` files, relative to the global directory).
This repository's file sets the `private` profile, `terms = "nvim"` and `check = ["memory/sessions/*.md"]`.
`python3 scripts/session_redact.py --explain` lists the store, the project file, each setting with the layer it comes from and the files read by each layer (paths and entry counts); `--check` adds a line per layer under the categories made of lists, indented by two spaces.

A lists directory may contain (all optional): `profile` and `fleet-names.txt` (project and terms-dir layers), `spell/*.utf-8.add`, `redact-terms.txt` (`re:` lines are regexes, `include <file>` loads another file), `identity.txt`, `path-aliases.txt`, `fleet-repos.txt`, `private-repos.txt`, `public-repos.txt`, `github-owners.txt`; see the script's docstring.
The data in the global directory does not depend on the profile: the `public` profile always applies identity and path aliases, and a `private` project applies them only with `identity = "redact"` or `path-aliases = "redact"` in its project file.
This repository does not opt in yet: its committed transcripts hold no `[redacted:user_...]` marker, and S14 decides.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
#MISE description="Export and redact the session transcript into memory/sessions/ (through a file, never a pipe)"
"""Usage: mise run session:export [--session ses_...] [--slug S<N>-<change-id>] [--dest DIR] [--no-children]
Close protocol step. Uses [redacted:repo]'s exporter ([redacted:repo]_ROOT, default [redacted:repo]) because it
produced the committed S0 and S1 transcripts and handles subagent sessions;
`opencode export` loses its tail when piped, so the exporter writes files.
Raw exports contain private data: they go to a mode 0700 scratch directory that is
always deleted. Each file is redacted with scripts/session_redact.py and the result is
verified with its --check. The redactor runs in the project root, where it finds the
project's `.session-redact.toml` (profile, private-store directory, S18). The user reads the
redacted transcript before it is committed (`docs(sessions): export S<N>`); the task does
not commit.
"""
import argparse
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
for parent in Path(__file__).resolve().parents:
    if (parent / "lib" / "workflow").is_dir():
        sys.path.insert(0, str(parent / "lib"))
        break
from workflow import herdr, roadmap, settings  # noqa: E402
def die(message: str) -> int:
    print(f"session:export: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1
def default_slug(root: Path, environ: dict) -> str | None:
    session = environ.get("ROADMAP_SESSION")
    change = environ.get("ROADMAP_CHANGE_ID")
    if session and not change:
        try:
            change = roadmap.parse((root / "ROADMAP.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).sessions[session].change_id
        except (OSError, KeyError, roadmap.RoadmapError):
            change = None
    return f"{session}-{change}" if session and change else None
def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="session:export", description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--session", help="opencode session id (default: the session of this herdr pane)")
    parser.add_argument("--slug", help="S<N>-<change-id> (default from ROADMAP_SESSION)")
    parser.add_argument("--dest", help="output directory (default memory/sessions)")
    parser.add_argument("--no-children", action="store_true", help="skip subagent sessions")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    environ = dict(os.environ)
    root = settings.project_root(environ)
    exporter = Path(environ.get("[redacted:repo]_ROOT", "[redacted:repo]")).expanduser() / "scripts" / "session" / "export.py"
    if not exporter.is_file():
        return die(f"[redacted:repo]'s exporter not found at {exporter} (set [redacted:repo]_ROOT)")
    redactor = root / "scripts" / "session_redact.py"
    if not redactor.is_file():
        return die(f"{redactor} not found")
    session_id = args.session or ((herdr.current_pane() or {}).get("agent_session") or {}).get("value")
    if not session_id:
        return die("cannot find the opencode session id: pass --session ses_...")
    slug = args.slug or default_slug(root, environ)
    if not slug:
        return die("cannot derive the slug: pass --slug S<N>-<change-id> or set ROADMAP_SESSION")
    dest = Path(args.dest) if args.dest else root / "memory" / "sessions"
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

```

Two folders in each checkout, ignored by git:

| Folder | Purpose | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| `.state/<agent>/` | durable: `state.md`, `snapshots/`, logs, notes, briefs, helper scripts, evidence | kept |
| `.tmp/<agent>/` | disposable: sandboxes, scratch clones, downloads, raw exports | deleted at will; gone when a worktree is removed |

- **Orchestrator:** `[redacted:repo]:.state/rog-orch/` and `.tmp/rog-orch/`.
- **Workers:** they use `.state/<name>/` and `.tmp/<name>/` inside their own worktree. That's inside their project, so writing there triggers no external-directory prompts and they never touch `main`.
  - When a worker retires, I copy its `.state/<name>/` into the main checkout's `.state/<name>/`, then remove the worktree, which takes its `.tmp/` with it.
- **The state file:** I'd use `.state/rog-orch/state.md` as the living current state, rewritten at each milestone. Frozen handoffs go in `.state/rog-orch/snapshots/<YYYYMMDDHHMM>-<why>.md`, starting with `…-pre-compaction.md`.
  - `status` reads like a progress report, and `snapshot` implies frozen, hence the split.
- **Caveats** (documented in `AGENTS.md` by the plumbing PR):
  - `git clean -fdx` or `-X` deletes both folders.
  - Sandboxes under `.tmp/` must have their own git root, which `box.sh` creates. Otherwise opencode would treat the enclosing checkout as the project and load its `opencode.json` (`"plugin": ["."]`).
  - prettier, oxlint, rg and opencode's search tools all respect `.gitignore`.
- **Immediately:** add `.state/` and `.tmp/` to `.git/info/exclude`. It's shared by every worktree and is local only, so I can move files before the PR is merged. The deploy preflight would otherwise see them as untracked.

I'm settling on how the state file should be updated: after every event, with a "Now" section for current status and an append-only journal that absorbs the existing permission log, and I'm checking that the extra updates are a small cost worth paying for crash and compaction safety.

I'm explaining what I meant by "frozen handoffs": a copy of the state file taken at a boundary, like before compaction, that never changes afterward. Since the live file keeps updating and a journal already records history, I'm leaning toward dropping snapshots, with the "Now" section and journal being enough, and making sure state.md is current before compaction.

I'm sketching the layout I'd propose: one ignored root per agent with a `state.md` holding a live "Now" section, an append-only journal of events, working folders, and a `tmp/` scratch directory that can be deleted anytime. I'm also thinking about promoting curated notes into committed memory, though I'm still undecided on which of the signal notes and step-4 inputs belong there.

I'm laying out the update rule: after every state-changing action, I'll touch the "Now" section of state.md and append a journal line before waiting or ending a turn. I'm also noting that worker folders get harvested into main's .state minus tmp/ at retirement, and that the question of whether signal notes belong in committed memory stays open until the later steps.

I'm noting that the main checkout's `.state` sticks around as long as the checkout does and survives reboots, though not a `git clean -X`, and it isn't backed up unless the user's backups cover ~/Work. The worktree's `.state` is the ephemeral one that gets harvested. Next I'm asking the user to approve the revised layout.


Here are the answers, with the plan revised to match.

**1. Option 2 (scratch under `.state/<agent>/tmp/`): pros and cons**
- **Pros:**
  - one ignored root and one convention
  - retiring a worker means copying a single folder, minus `tmp/`
  - one place to back up or exclude
- **Cons:**
  - durable and disposable files share a tree, so cleanup must target `tmp/` exactly; a careless `rm -rf .state/<agent>` loses real state
  - backups of `.state/` pick up gigabytes of scratch unless they exclude `*/tmp/`

  If valuable content gets promoted out of `.state/` (see 2), the cons are small. **I now recommend option 2.**

**2. Are both ephemeral? What is worth keeping?**
- **In a worktree:** yes, they die with it. That's why worker state is copied into the main checkout before a worktree is removed.
- **In the main checkout:** they last as long as that checkout. They survive reboots, unlike `/tmp`'s 10-day cleanup, but not `git clean -X`, and backups only include them if yours cover `~/Work`.
- **Most content is already elsewhere:**
  - PR bodies and decisions are on GitHub.
  - Briefs are inside the session transcripts (exported to `memory/sessions/`).
  - The evidence is summarized in the PRs.
- **What exists nowhere else:**
  - the orchestrator's live state
  - the decision journal (`answers.log`, with my reasons)
  - two curated notes (`signal-notes.md`, `step4-inputs.md`)
  - tooling that has no home yet (`watch`/`once`, `deploy-main.sh`, `tally.mjs`)
- **What should happen to them:**
  - `.state/` should be working state, not the archive.
  - The curated notes should eventually move into committed, redacted memory, the way [redacted:repo] has `memory/notes`, `lessons` and `studies`.
  - The tools should move into a repo.
  - Where they go is part of step 4 and the [redacted:repo] phase 8 signal.

**3. Update frequency:** agreed, it should be updated far more often. The new rule: after every state change and before every wait or turn end, I update the file.
- State changes include a prompt sent, a permission answered, a PR opened or merged, a deploy, a decision or an incident.
- Then you can read it at any moment, and a crash or compaction loses at most one step.

**4. "Frozen handoffs":** I meant a dated copy of the state file, written at a boundary such as this compaction and never edited again, so you could later see what I knew at that moment. With a continuously updated file plus an append-only journal, that is redundant. **I'm dropping snapshots.**

# Revised layout
```
.state/<agent>/            ignored by git (.git/info/exclude now, .gitignore in the plumbing PR)
  state.md                 "Now": situation, workers, open items, next action; rewritten at every change
  journal.md               append-only, timestamped one-liners: prompts, approvals (replaces answers.log), PRs, merges, deploys, decisions, incidents
  notes/                   signal-notes.md, step4-inputs.md (to be promoted to committed memory later)
  bin/  briefs/            working tools and briefs
  tmp/                     disposable: sandboxes (own git root), scratch clones, raw exports (0700); delete any time
```
- **Workers:** the same layout inside their own worktree. When a worker retires, I copy its `.state/<name>/` without `tmp/` to the main checkout's `.state/<name>/`.

**Order of work, unchanged otherwise:**
0. identity, `info/exclude`, deploy batch 3
1. move files from `/tmp/opencode/rog` (journal seeded from `answers.log`), fix paths and self-test, delete `/tmp` scratch
2. plumbing PR (merge 1 is yours)
3. sessions export PR (merge 2 is yours, after you read the files)
4. `state.md` brought fully up to date; then you compact

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Redact private data from a session transcript (Markdown).

TRANSITIONAL: [redacted:repo] T-063 covers secrets only (study B-035: private terms,
paths and configuration layers are not planned there), so this script stays
until a [redacted:repo] tool covers the same ground (ROADMAP D23, S17).

Usage:
  session_redact.py [--profile private|public] < in.md > out.md
  session_redact.py [--profile private|public] --check [FILE...]
  session_redact.py [--profile private|public] --explain

No private term lives in this script, nor in any repository. Terms live in
the private store (default ~/.local/share/[redacted:private], a clone of a
private repository; SESSION_REDACT_STORE overrides it) and are read in
layers, later layers winning for single settings and adding to the lists:

  1. built-in defaults (profile private, fleet names redacted, identity and
     path aliases 'auto');
  2. global: <store>/session-redact/, the user's own data for every project:
     list files and an optional config.toml (profile, fleet-names, identity,
     path-aliases, spell);
  3. project: .session-redact.toml at the git root (settings only, never a
     term: profile, terms, fleet-names, identity, path-aliases, check,
     exclude) and the directory of the store it names with 'terms';
  4. SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR, a directory of list files read as one more
     layer ('terms-dir'); the command line of earlier consumers;
  5. --profile.

With no global directory, no project file and no SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR,
the project directory is <store>/nvim (the behaviour before the layers). The
script stops with status 2 when nothing is configured, when a named
directory is missing or when a configuration file is invalid: it never
redacts less than configured.

A lists directory may contain (all optional):

  profile            'private' or 'public' (project and terms-dir layers)
  fleet-names.txt    'keep' or 'redact' (same layers): whether fleet
                     repository names stay readable in the public profile
  spell/*.add        private words, one per line ('#' comments, '/flags';
                     'word/!' marks a misspelled word and is ignored)
  redact-terms.txt   one term per line; 're:' prefix = regex;
                     'include <relative path>' loads another file
  identity.txt       '<category>: <value>' lines about the user (fullname,
                     firstname, lastname, email, username, ...); each
                     becomes [redacted:user_<category>]
  path-aliases.txt   '<~/path> = <name>' lines; the path becomes
                     [redacted:<name>] (for example a worktrees root)
  fleet-repos.txt    repository names under ~/Work; 'tries' means
                     [redacted:repo]>
  private-repos.txt  more private repository names (public profile)
  public-repos.txt   public repositories, allowed as 'owner/name'
  github-owners.txt  GitHub owners; any 'owner/name' not in public-repos
                     is redacted (default deny)

Lists are the union of the layers, each entry once, owned by the first layer
that defines it; a layer can add an entry and cannot remove one.

Profiles:
  private  transcripts kept in a private repository. Fleet references
           ~/Work/<repo>/<path> become `<repo>:<path>` ([redacted:repo] DR-012).
  public   transcripts for a public repository. Also redacts private
           repository names, credential variable names, token-scope
           lines, IPv4 addresses, e-mail addresses and non-public git
           hosts, and always applies identity and path aliases. With
           fleet-names 'keep', fleet repositories stay readable in the
           DR-012 form (names of private repositories are then published:
           a decision of the repository owner).
  The private profile applies identity and path aliases only when the
  setting 'identity' or 'path-aliases' is 'redact'.

Rules, in this order:
  1. secrets (API keys, tokens, age secret keys, JWTs, private key blocks)
     become [redacted:secret];
  2. /home/<user> becomes ~ (not /home/linuxbrew, Homebrew's prefix, nor
     the placeholder /home/user);
  3. identity values become [redacted:user_<category>];
  4. terms become [redacted:private];
  5. path aliases;
  6. fleet paths, then, in the public profile, GitHub slugs, bare
     repository names and the generic public rules.

--check prints counts per category, never the terms, and exits 1 if
anything is left; under the categories made of lists it adds a line per
layer that owns entries (indented by two spaces). Without FILE it checks the
project's 'check' globs minus 'exclude'. --explain prints the store, the
project file, each setting with its source and the files read by layer
(paths and entry counts, never a term). The output is deterministic and
idempotent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os

import sys

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

PROFILES = ("private", "public")
FLEET_NAMES = ("keep", "redact")
OPT_INS = ("auto", "redact")
MAX_INCLUDE_DEPTH = 3

STORE_ENV = "SESSION_REDACT_STORE"
TERMS_DIR_ENV = "SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR"
GLOBAL_DIRNAME = "session-redact"
LEGACY_DIRNAME = "nvim"
PROJECT_FILE = ".session-redact.toml"
GLOBAL_KEYS = {"profile", "fleet-names", "identity", "path-aliases", "spell"}

        - hk.pkl gets exclude = List("memory/sessions/**") on trailing_whitespace and newlines, via (Builtins.x) { exclude = ... }. The directory
          exclude makes the README unchecked by those two steps, but prettier and .editorconfig cover it.
        - prettier gets the same exclude, so hk does not hand ignored files to it. I will check whether that is needed.
        - detect_private_key and check_merge_conflict stay on everything. Oxlint is n/a because it only globs code files.
     4. Docs: memory/sessions/README.md, an AGENTS.md section "State, scratch and transcripts" (at most 15 lines, plus memory/ in the map), and one
        sentence in CONTRIBUTING.md. No CHANGELOG or TODO change.

       description or commit messages. I will write "the fleet's session exporter (export.py --sanitize)" and "the fleet's redactor". The redactor
       path ~/.config/nvim/scripts/session_redact.py passes untouched, so I will give it once as the example. I will run the redactor over the README
       and the PR body before publishing. Shall I go with that? If you want the names published, that is the owner decision the fleet-names = "keep"

     - No secrets scanner in hk.pkl. Only detect_private_key is there. The redactor --check is the real gate, and it is local only because the terms

+## State, scratch and transcripts
+
+- An agent keeps its durable state (notes, helper scripts) in `.state/<agent>/` and disposable scratch in
+  `.state/<agent>/tmp/`. Both are ignored by git, never published, and private to that agent. `.tmp/` is ignored too.
+- Nothing durable in `/tmp`: it is cleaned after days and lost at reboots.
+- `git clean -X` and `git clean -fdx` delete ignored files, `.state/` included: not in a checkout whose state you keep.
+- A sandbox that runs git or opencode (outside the tests, which use `sandbox()`) needs its own git root (`git init`),
+  or they take the enclosing checkout as the project.
+- Never commit a raw session export. Transcripts go to `memory/sessions/` redacted, by the procedure in its README.md:
+  the repository is public, and what is committed cannot be unpublished.
+

@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+# Session transcripts
+
+Redacted transcripts of the maintainer's orchestration and work sessions with coding agents. They are history, not
+documentation: they record what was tried and decided at the time, and may be wrong or superseded.
+[README.md](../../README.md), [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and the code are
+the source of truth.
+
+## Naming
+
+`YYYYMMDDHHMM-<slug>.md`: the start of the session, then a short lowercase slug with hyphens.
+
+## Adding a transcript
+
+1. Export the session with the fleet's session exporter (`export.py --sanitize`), with `--out-dir` pointing to a
+   directory of mode `0700` under `.state/<agent>/tmp/` (`install -d -m 0700 .state/<agent>/tmp/export`), never to this
+   repository.
+2. Redact it with the fleet's redactor in its `public` profile, for example
+   `python3 ~/.config/nvim/scripts/session_redact.py --profile public < raw.md > memory/sessions/<name>.md`.
+3. Run the redactor with `--check` from the repository root. It reads `.session-redact.toml` (settings only, no term)
+   and exits 1 if anything is left in `memory/sessions/*.md`. This gate is local: the terms it uses are private, so CI
+   cannot run it.
+4. The maintainer reads the redacted file before it is committed.
+
+## Why raw exports are never committed
+
+A raw export holds what the redactor removes: secrets, private repository and host names, addresses, local paths and
+personal data. The repository is public and Git history cannot be unpublished, so the only file that may reach a commit
+is the redacted one. Delete raw exports once the redacted file is accepted; `.state/` and `.tmp/` are ignored by Git.
+
+## Tooling
+
+This directory is left alone by prettier and by the whitespace and newline hooks: a transcript keeps what the tools
+printed, trailing spaces and very long lines included. The private key and merge conflict checks still apply. The npm
+package publishes a whitelist of files (`files` in `package.json`) that does not include `memory/`.

```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
session:export — Exporte une session OpenCode en Markdown, conforme au gabarit
natif `/export`, sous la convention de nommage
`memory/sessions/{YYYYMMDDHHMM}[-{id}]-{slug}.md`.

Contexte : ADR-201 (convention de nommage, trailers, merge porteur) ; T-622 (dépôt
d'origine) ; `{id}` optionnel introduit en T-113 (ADR-201 v1.6.0).

OpenCode ne fournit ni export Markdown en CLI, ni option de nom de fichier
(`opencode export <id>` renvoie du JSON brut sur stdout — cf. `opencode export --help`).
Ce script :

  1. Lit la session par la couche `lib.py.sessions.session`, qui appelle `opencode export
     <SESSION_ID>` (contrat CLI documenté et stable) par l'adaptateur du harnais
     (`lib.py.harness.opencode`, `T-279a`, `CT-007`, `CT-008`) : ce script ne connaît que le
     modèle normalisé d'une session, jamais le document brut.
  2. Reconstruit le Markdown selon le gabarit natif de `/export` (dialogue TUI),
     identifié par analyse du binaire OpenCode (fonctions internes non documentées,
     susceptibles d'évoluer entre versions) — le contrat stable dont ce script dépend
     reste celui, documenté, de `opencode export` (JSON), pas ces internes.
  3. Détermine le nom de fichier `{created:%Y%m%d%H%M}[-{id}]-{slug}.md` :
       - `--slug` fourni  → utilisé tel quel (recommandé pour respecter précisément
         la convention `P{n}-M{n}-sujet` observée dans memory/sessions/ existants).
       - sinon            → heuristique de pertinence sur le titre de session actuel
         (cf. `title_is_pertinent`) :
           - pertinent     → slug dérivé automatiquement du titre (slugify), avec
             extraction d'un éventuel préfixe `{ID}-` (`T-NNN`/`M-NNN`/`D-NNN`/
             `H-NNN`, cf. `split_id_prefix`) préservé **verbatim** dans le nom de
             fichier plutôt que slugifié.
           - non pertinent → échec explicite invitant à fournir `--slug` ou
             `--rename "Titre court et synthétique"`.
  4. `--rename TITLE` : renomme la session en base *avant* d'exporter et dérive
     le slug (et l'éventuel `{id}`) de ce nouveau titre (cf.
     `lib.py.sessions.session.rename_session` pour le mécanisme et son repli automatique en
     cas d'échec).

`--last` (résolution automatique, cf. T-623, dépôt d'origine) : dispense de fournir
SESSION_ID en résolvant la session la plus récemment active *de ce dépôt*
(cf. `lib.py.sessions.session.resolve_last_session`). Réservé à l'usage humain interactif ou aux
orchestrations mono-agent (ex. `task:close`) : un agent connaît son propre
SESSION_ID et doit le passer explicitement plutôt que s'appuyer sur `--last`,
qui reste ambigu en cas d'exécution concurrente (sous-agents, autres fenêtres
OpenCode sur ce dépôt) — cf. §Garde d'ambiguïté dans
`lib.py.sessions.session.resolve_last_session`.

Paramétrisation pour les consommateurs délégants (T-304, ADR-201 §Traçabilité de
session v1.23.0) : `--directory DIR` substitue le répertoire de résolution
(défaut REPO_ROOT inchangé) ; `--last-warn` assouplit la garde d'ambiguïté
`[GIT-10]` en avertissement stderr plutôt qu'échec dur (défaut absent inchangé).
Les deux nécessitent `--last`/`--resolve-last` (erreur explicite sinon).

Export incrémental (T-140, ADR-201 §Export incrémental de session, v1.14.0) :
`--since (auto|MSG_ID)` n'exporte que la partie du transcript à partir d'un message
donné, borne **inclusive** (le message est réémis complet — il pouvait être en vol,
donc incomplet, dans l'export antérieur qu'il chaîne). `auto` recherche, dans
`--out-dir`, l'export existant le plus avancé de la même session (marqueur
`<!-- session-export: through <msg_id> -->` en priorité, dérivation par
correspondance de préfixe en repli pour les exports hérités sans marqueur) ; en
l'absence de tout export antérieur, bascule silencieusement en export complet.
.venv/bin/python -> ~/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python  64B

PR #16 is the second merge, and it's yours. It adds 10 session transcripts, 126,602 lines (6.5 MB), one commit per session, and CI is green including GitGuardian. Please read them in workspace `rog-export` (hunk) before approving, because history can't be unpublished.

**What I found while exporting**
- **`--sanitize` empties the transcript.** `opencode export --sanitize` replaces every message, reasoning block and tool input with placeholders, so the export reads like `[redacted:text:prt_…]` throughout. I exported without it and let the public redactor do the work.
- **The redactor missed a few things** that I caught with my own scan. All were present in the first pass.
  - A hostname from your SSH setup, 93 times. It came from the `rog-rules` log analysis and the samples in my own session.
  - Two private project names, `[redacted:private]` and `[redacted:private]`, plus `[redacted:private]`.
  - 41 NUL bytes from my `rg -a` search of the opencode and hk binaries, which made git treat my transcript as binary.
- **How I fixed them:** a scrub step after the redactor, in `bin/export-sessions.sh`. Its extra terms live in `.state/rog-orch/private/extra-terms.txt`, which is ignored by git. This session's file is now plain text with no private terms.
- **Residuals I left alone:**
  - tool names such as `insync`, `nextcloud`, `chezmoi` and `obsidian`, which appear in this repo's own test cases and rule discussions
  - your GitHub login, already in `package.json`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the schemas
  - `git@gitlab.com`, a public documentation host
